To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in acute leukemia the degree of PGP expression, measured by the mean fluorescence intensity (MFI) with MRK- 16 monoclonal antibody correlates with anthradycline retention and sensitivity.
the MFI with the anti-Pgp monoclonal MRK-16 is a reliable and easy to perform test that may be useful to assess Pgp related MDR in acute leukemia.
the degree of P170 glycoproteine expression, as measured by the intensity of reaction with the anti-Pgp monoclonal MRK-16, correlates with anthradycline retention and cytotoxicity in leukemic cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the definition of the threshold of Pgp overexpression that is related with a significant decrease in the sensitivity to anthradyclines of leukemic cells.
the study of the Pgp expression and its relationship with the cell response to anthracycline treatment in acute leukemia.

the study of Pgp-related drug resistance in leukemia, in order to identify the degree of P gp expression that is associated with a decrease in the sensitivity of the leukemic cells to chemotherapy and with the identification of a quick method of Pgp determination in leukemic blasts that is suitable for clinical use.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the degree of PGP expression is a determinant of the sensitivity of leukemia cells to anthracycline, and this is the reason why the PGP expression is considered to be a marker of multidrug resistance.
a high MFI with MRk-16 is indicative of a high Pgp expression in leukemic cells and is associated with a reduced anthracycline sensitivity.
the Pgp-related MFI is the most reliable indicator of the Pgp-related resistance to anthracycline drugs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a high MFI with MRk-16 correlates with a low anthracycline sensitivity, and this in turn correlates with a high retention of the drug.
the degree of the MRK16 reaction correlates with the degree of anthracycline cytotoxicity and with anthracycline retention.
a high degree of reactivity of leukemic cells to MRK- 16 correlates with a high degree of resistance of leukemic cells in vitro to anthracycline drugs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Pgp expression level in acute leukemic cells can be estimated by measuring the intensity of the MRk-16 staining.
the intensity of the cell reaction to MRK- 16 correlates with anthracyclin retention, which, in turn, correlates with cell cytotoxicity.
the degree of P170 expression is more important than the number of cells expressing P170 in determining cell sensitivity to chemotherapy.
